biography: Tiel Andrade, born in the vibrant heart of São Paulo, Brazil, carries the rhythm of samba and the spirit of motorsport in his blood. His journey began not on the asphalt, but on the dusty karting tracks of Interlagos, a gift from his grandfather, a former mechanic for Emerson Fittipaldi. Tiel showed early promise, mastering the art of defensive driving, a skill honed from years of battling more experienced rivals with inferior equipment. A defining moment came at the Brazilian Karting Championship in 2008, where he held off a relentless attack from a future Formula 1 driver to secure a podium finish, proving his mettle under pressure. After a stint in Formula 3 Sudamericana, funded by a local sugar cane magnate, Tiel transitioned to prototype racing, finding a home with MetalMoro, piloting their MRX Honda P3. While he hasn't reached the pinnacle of motorsport, his tenacity and strategic prowess make him a formidable competitor.
drivingStyle: Andrade is a master of defensive driving, prioritizing consistency and tire management above all else. He's known for his late braking and ability to position his car perfectly to discourage overtaking, often frustrating more aggressive drivers. He conserves his tires early in the race, allowing him to push harder in the final stages when others are struggling. While not the fastest qualifier, his race pace is consistently strong, and he excels in endurance events, a testament to his calculated approach.

careerHighlight: Winning the 6 Hours of Curitiba in 2021, after a masterful display of fuel conservation and defensive driving in the closing stages, holding off a charging field on older tires.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final hour of the 12 Hours of Tarumã in 2020 due to a mechanical failure, costing his team a likely victory.
